title: Does Beauty Pay? An Analysis of College Athlete Name, Image, and Likeness (NIL) Pricing
affiliations: Bowdoin College and Bowdoin College - Department of Economics

detail.title: Does Beauty Pay? An Analysis of College Athlete Name, Image, and Likeness (NIL) Pricing

declarations.ethicsApproval: The survey that is summarized in this paper was approved by Bowdoin College's Institutional Review Board.
declarations.funderStatement: Erik Nelson funded this research with his own research fund.

detail.abstract: Recent court decisions mean that US college athletes can monetize their name, image, and likeness (NIL) and remain eligible to play their sport. The NIL market has quickly become a multi-billion-dollar industry. However, the determinants of athletes' NIL values have not yet been identified. We address this knowledge gap by estimating a wage system model over a dataset of college athletes that combines their published NIL prices, their characteristics, including perceived attractiveness and trustworthiness, and information on the schools they play for. We find that expertise at sport is the most important driver of NIL prices. "Superstar" athletes-those college athletes most expert at their sport-set much higher NIL prices than their more "Conventional" peers. Within both classes of athletes, the size of an athlete's social media audience explains much of the variation in their NIL prices. However, that is where the similarities in the NIL price generating process between the two classes of athletes end. Whereas Superstars' NIL prices tend to increase in athletic ability, Conventional athletes' NIL prices are not influenced by their sporting abilities. Instead, the Conventional athlete's NIL prices increase in their school's enrollment and their perceived attractiveness: a one standard deviation (SD) increase in a Conventional athlete's attractiveness score increases their NIL prices, on average, by 10 percent, all else equal. And counter to previous findings in the economics of endorsement literature, Conventional athletes that are judged more trustworthy charge less for their NIL: a one SD increase in a Conventional athlete's trustworthiness score decreases their NIL prices, on average, by 9 percent, all else equal. Given that an athlete's perceived attractiveness affects their NIL market value, we identify athlete characteristics that are most associated with high attractiveness. Based on a survey of 805 people, we find that the public rates female athletes significantly more attractive than male athletes. Further, there is some evidence that beholders find athletes who match their race and their preferred sexual gender a bit more attractive, all else equal. NIL market regulators are using a proprietary algorithm to judge the appropriateness of NIL prices. This algorithm does not account for an athlete's perceived attractiveness or trustworthiness. Therefore, the regulator's opinion of appropriate NIL prices deviates from what the market is willing to pay for many athletes' NIL.

title: How People Actually Use Generative AI: An Integrative Analysis of Real-World Use-Cases

detail.title: How People Actually Use Generative AI: An Integrative Analysis of Real-World Use-Cases
detail.abstract:
Generative artificial intelligence (AI) has rapidly diffused across professional and personal contexts, yet empirical understanding of how these systems are actually used remains fragmented. Existing evidence is dispersed across qualitative narratives, largescale behavioral analyses, and task-based occupational studies, each offering partial insight into real-world use. This paper integrates three complementary empirical sources-a qualitative taxonomy of human-reported use-cases, large-scale behavioral data from millions of AI interactions, and task-level mappings to standardized occupational activities-to develop a unified framework for understanding generative AI use in practice.
Across datasets, we find strong convergence around a core set of activities: writing and editing, information retrieval, explanation and teaching, ideation, and decision support. These uses are concentrated in knowledge-intensive work and are overwhelmingly augmentative rather than fully automating, with humans remaining firmly in the loop. Generative AI functions primarily as cognitive infrastructure that supports thinking, communication, and judgment rather than as an autonomous replacement for labor. At the same time, important divergences across sources-such as the prominence of companionship in qualitative narratives versus its low prevalence in behavioral datahighlight how methodological lenses shape observed patterns. 
Building on these findings, we propose a unified framework that characterizes generative AI use along three dimensions: functional activity, relational role between human and AI, and degree of automation versus augmentation. The framework reconciles heterogeneous evidence and provides a task-centered lens for future research on the economic, organizational, and societal implications of generative AI.

title: Luxury's DNA: A Systematic Review of Brand Attributes and Transfer Strategies

detail.title: Luxury's DNA: A Systematic Review of Brand Attributes and Transfer Strategies
detail.abstract: Purpose-This systematic review addresses the translation gap between luxury brand management and mainstream categories, examining the transferability of luxury elements and the conditions under which it occurs. Despite extensive luxury scholarship and emerging premiumisation, theoretical fragmentation persists: luxury research remains confined within its sector, while mainstream brand studies lack grounding in luxury theory. Design/methodology/approach-Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, we systematically reviewed 23 peer-reviewed articles from 2015-2025 in Scopus, Web of Science, and Business Source Complete. Through narrative synthesis across seven themes, we analyzed luxury attributes, exclusivity mechanisms, and transferability conditions. Findings-The results reveal transferability through three layers. Layer 1 (universal brand equity principles) shows full transferability across categories. Layer 2 (strategic codes: artificial scarcity, experiential orchestration, digital stratification, sustainability integration) requires authentic symbolic translation, not superficial imitation. Layer 3 (cultural legitimacy: historical heritage, institutional consecration, extreme craftsmanship) resists replication due to temporal requirements. Cross-cultural findings show that transferability varies: Western consumers prioritize subtle refinement, while emerging markets favor conspicuous signalling, moderating successful adoption strategies. Originality/value-This review provides a systematic integration of luxury-to-mainstream transferability, proposing a three-layer framework that resolves the theoretical ambiguity regarding which elements can be adapted versus resisting replication. This study advances 2 luxury brand management theory by showing that luxury's strategic essence is layered rather than monolithic, while offering evidence-based premiumization guidance for aspirational brands.

title: Enriching Digital Sport Marketing Communication: Examining Emoji Functions Through Media Richness Theory
affiliations: University of Colorado, Colorado Springs, Brock University, University of Arizona - Eller College of Management, University of Colorado, Colorado Springs and University of Arizona - Eller College of Management

detail.title: Enriching Digital Sport Marketing Communication: Examining Emoji Functions Through Media Richness Theory
detail.abstract: This study extends Media Richness Theory (MRT) by examining how emojis function as nonverbal cues in digital sport communication. This was accomplished through a mixed-method approach combining machine learning and quantitative content analysis of 13,642 X (formerly Twitter) posts from professional sport teams. The study aimed to understand how emojis function within sport organizations' digital messaging and to identify contextual factors that influence emoji interpretation in sport digital communication. Our findings indicate that emojis serve dual functions: (i) as replacements for textual content and (ii) as supplements that reinforce emotional resonance with the classification models, achieving higher accuracy for singleemoji (80.3% F1-score) versus multi-emoji messages (72.2%). Contextual elements, including immediate textual surroundings and broader sport situations, significantly shape emoji interpretation and effectiveness. Results show that strategic emoji usage patterns vary across game situations, team performance contexts, and marketing-related announcements. This research offers theoretical contributions by extending MRT to account for nonverbal digital cues while providing foundational understanding to inform sport marketing strategies. The findings establish patterns of emoji functionality that future research can build upon to directly measure consumer response and marketing outcomes across diverse sport contexts.

title: Strategic Implementation of an 'Event Lottery' System to Maximize Fan Experience and Brand Loyalty: Focusing on Gamification and Prospect Theory

detail.title: Strategic Implementation of an 'Event Lottery' System to Maximize Fan Experience and Brand Loyalty: Focusing on Gamification and Prospect Theory
detail.abstract: This study proposes the 'Event Lottery' system, an innovative marketing framework designed to maximize the emotional immersion of fans within the sports industry and build long-term brand loyalty. In the contemporary sports consumption environment, fans have evolved from passive spectators into active participants who contribute to the creation of brand value. This strategy is designed by integrating Gamification, Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) & Reciprocity, Expectation-Enhancement, and Prospect Theory. The proposed system focuses on immediate emotional intervention through pre-game minigames, continuous immersion via mid-game lottery drawings, and the reinforcement of brand equity through the social return of a portion of the proceeds. This study suggests that such implicit persuasion and emotional immersion strategies reduce consumers' cognitive resistance and form a deeper connection between the brand and its fans

publicationDetails.detailsText: Kilts Center at Chicago Booth Marketing Data Center Paper

detail.abstract: This paper investigates market power and consumer inertia in the vaping and tobacco industry, with a focus on substitution patterns between cigarettes and e-cigarettes in the context of market structure changes, including a merger between cigarette and e-cigarette companies and a potential total ban on traditional tobacco. Using a structural demand and supply framework, we leverage both aggregate retail scanner data and household-level panel data to capture consumer heterogeneity and state dependence, examining how past choices influence current preferences. Our merger simulations indicate that both vaping and cigarette brands experience higher prices and lower sales, leading to a 0.72% decline in consumer surplus and a 1.05% increase in smoking-attributable health costs (SAHC) due to substitution to other firms. In the scenario of a total ban, e-cigarette prices rise alongside sales. These results provide insights into competitive dynamics and the policy implications of a consolidating nicotine market.

title: From Syntax to Semantics: The Rise of the Taste-based Economy and Viral Creation Loops in Intent-Driven Software Generation

detail.title: From Syntax to Semantics: The Rise of the Taste-based Economy and Viral Creation Loops in Intent-Driven Software Generation
detail.abstract: The emergence of "Vibe Coding"-a paradigm where developers guide AI systems through natural language intent rather than explicit syntax-represents a fundamental shift in software engineering. This transformation is not merely technical but economic: as Large Language Models (LLMs) commoditize programming skills, the locus of value creation shifts from syntactic mastery to semantic judgment, or what we term "taste." This paper introduces the Taste-Based Economy framework to explain how early-stage startups can build sustainable competitive advantages when marginal production costs approach zero. Through a multiple case study analysis of three leading AI-native development platforms-Cursor, Replit, and Lovable-we identify three distinct Go-to-Market (GTM) archetypes: Flow-Led Growth, Remix-Led Growth, and Creation-Led Growth. Our findings reveal that traditional technology moats are dissolving, replaced by new barriers centered on curation capability and viral creation loops. We introduce the concept of "Intent Bandwidth" to measure human-AI communication efficiency and propose a "Creativity Multiplier" metric for quantifying viral growth in generative software markets. This research contributes to marketing theory by extending Bourdieu's cultural capital framework to AI-native markets and offers practical implications for founders, venture capitalists, and platform designers navigating the post-code economy.

title: The Theory of Participative Value

detail.title: The Theory of Participative Value

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial or personal interests that could have influenced the research presented in this paper.

The theory is derived from observation of publicly available interactions and does not include intervention, experimentation, or collection of personal data.

detail.abstract:
This paper introduces the Theory of Participative Value, a field-derived conceptual framework that explains a specific pattern of user behavior observed in publicly communicated pricing decisions. Traditional pricing models assume that price increases inherently generate resistance and are primarily evaluated through transactional cost–benefit logic. However, field observation reveals contexts in which this assumption does not fully hold.

The theory is based on a publicly documented interaction in which an organization openly engaged its community regarding the acceptability of a potential price increase, without presenting the decision as predetermined. The observed responses exhibited normative support, public legitimation of the price adjustment, and a notable absence of conflict.

The Theory of Participative Value proposes that under conditions of long-term trust, demonstrated quality, and public inclusion in decision-making, a portion of users transitions from the role of consumers to that of normative value guardians. In this role, price sensitivity is reduced, and price increases are legitimized as mechanisms for preserving established standards.

The theory does not claim universal applicability, nor does it replace existing pricing models. It offers a complementary conceptual framework for understanding pricing behavior in trust-based, publicly engaged contexts.

detail.abstract:
Online dating companies have monetized and capitalized on the idea of finding love, creating a billion-dollar industry matching individuals with their “soul mates.” With its perks and benefits, the online love industry is not without risk. Despite some dating companies limiting user eligibility in their terms and conditions to those without felony and sexual offense convictions, there is no actual screening process established by these companies. Furthermore, there are no uniform safety protocols among dating app companies. This lack of uniformity coupled with access to all, including violent offenders, allows repeat offenders to engage in “delightful” conversations with unsuspecting strangers across the globe.

Since the rise in popularity of online dating, there have been several instances of violent offenses, ranging from rape to murder, stemming from multiple dating apps. With the steady increase in violent crimes on the web, online dating companies promising a fairy-tale ending have not upheld their end of the deal with their customers. Now that using online dating apps has become more prevalent in today’s society and with the changing landscape of section 230 of the Communications Decency Act—which precludes software providers from liability for information placed on their sites or activities occurring through the use of their sites as long as they are acting as passive conduits—companies should utilize a uniform safety protocol to make their dating sites safer for users.

title: Quality Forecasting and Reliability Modeling in Expansive .NET Application Landscapes

detail.title: Quality Forecasting and Reliability Modeling in Expansive .NET Application Landscapes
detail.abstract: Quality forecasting and reliability modeling offer a pathway to strengthen engineering decision making across expansive .NET application landscapes that have grown in scale, interconnectedness, and operational sensitivity within contemporary enterprise environments. Large .NET ecosystems often accumulate complex dependency chains, heterogeneous architectural layers, and uneven instrumentation coverage, which collectively increase the probability of latent defects, performance regressions, and reliability degradation that traditional quality assurance methods struggle to anticipate. The purpose of this research is to formulate and evaluate a structured framework that integrates historical software metrics, operational telemetry, release artifacts, and incident patterns to forecast quality risks and model reliability behavior before failures materialize. The methodological design combines multi source data aggregation, feature extraction grounded in software quality theory, and predictive modeling techniques suited for temporal and component level forecasting across distributed .NET services. Empirical observations suggest that the proposed framework offers meaningful gains in early warning capability, prediction stability across release cycles, and actionable risk segmentation for engineering teams responsible for large scale .NET systems. The analysis argues that integrating forecasting outputs into release readiness assessments and operational planning provides a pathway for reducing incident recurrence, improving allocation of testing and refactoring resources, and elevating long term system resilience. By articulating the conceptual, architectural, and empirical foundations of predictive quality engineering for .NET landscapes, this research contributes to academic discourse on software reliability modeling and offers practical guidance for enterprises seeking to modernize quality practices in environments where traditional inspection based approaches are insufficient for the scale and complexity of modern .NET applications.

title: OM FORUM From "Saving Africa" to "Learning from Africa": African Insights for Value Creation and Resilience

detail.abstract: Problem definition: Operations and Supply Chain Management (O&SCM) research in Africa has often focused on challenges stemming from socio-political factors, such as humanitarian logistics, famine, fragile procurement networks, poverty, and military conflicts. While valuable, this problem-centric framing often overlooks the African context as a rich source of conceptual and managerial innovation. Methodology/Results: This forum paper shifts the perspective, arguing that African organizational philosophies offer unique, meaningful, and scalable insights for the global O&SCM community. We introduce three foundational paradigms-Ubuntu (social inclusivity), Kgotla (participatory governance), and Bogosi (ethical stewardship)-as alternative frameworks for modern supply chain challenges. We explore the implications and applications of these paradigms for supply chain research and practice, providing illustrative models and highlighting their relevance to governance, resilience, and sustainable sourcing. Furthermore, we provide a framework that connects contextual problems from Africa and beyond to methodological imperatives in O&SCM, and we map them onto the United Nations (UN) Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), illustrating their relevance to both frontier and developed markets. Managerial insights: By examining these paradigms, we broaden the scope of O&SCM research, moving beyond a Western-centric focus and enriching the field with lessons derived from the African context as well as frontier lands. African practices, rooted in adaptability and inclusivity, offer precisely the insights needed to address today's global supply chain challenges. Our work suggests that the "theories of tomorrow" must integrate realities from the Global South to remain relevant. By embracing the spirit of Ubuntu, scholars can co-create a more equitable, resilient, and globally representative foundation for O&SCM research and practice.

title: Evaluation of the Effectiveness of Using Personalized Advertising on Facebook

detail.title: Evaluation of the Effectiveness of Using Personalized Advertising on Facebook
detail.abstract: In the age of information and communication technology, consumers' attitude toward the creativity of advertising messages is considered as one of the issues in the area of marketing, for which there is not too much information. Thus, the objective of this research was to evaluate the effectiveness of personalized advertising on Facebook. The research population included the Internet users and members of the Facebook social network in Iran, the exact number of which has not been announced. Given the unknown nature of the research population, a sample size of 384 people was randomly selected among Internet users. However, as we did not have a complete list of the target population in order to select the sample randomly, we used the convenient sampling method in this research. The only inclusion criterion of the study is being a member in Facebook. Based on the results obtained, all the hypotheses of the research were approved. In other words, development of a comprehensive model of using personalized advertising in social networks is effective in users' attitudes and behavioral responses (these attitudes and behavioral responses included the consumer perception of the personalization of advertising and advertising credibility, pessimism about advertising, avoiding them, as well as behavioral intentions of consumers with regard to using this advertising for purchasing).

publicationDetails.detailsText: Office of Financial Research Working Paper No. 26-03
publicationDetails.journalName: Office of Financial Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: This paper examines client clearing, which now accounts for the majority of risk managed in centrally cleared markets. Using confidential transaction-level data on credit default swaps, we show that client clearing enhances netting efficiency for dealers and generates pricing advantages for clients. Adoption of central clearing leads clients to expand their sets of dealer trading partners, thereby enhancing market access and competition. To access central counterparties, clients depend on clearing member firms, favoring those with stronger credit quality and with whom they have established trading relationships. Offering these services produces spillover benefits for member firms' market making activity by improving client retention and pricing power. Clients' reliance on clearing members creates operational fragilities under stress, especially for those with limited member relationships. Our findings provide novel insights about the economic consequences of client clearing and are particularly relevant given recent clearing mandates, most notably in U.S. Treasury markets.

detail.abstract: Adaptive User Interfaces (AUIs) have become increasingly essential as modern software applications are expected to deliver seamless, intuitive, and personalized experiences across a broad spectrum of devices, screen dimensions, accessibility needs, and interaction contexts. With users frequently transitioning between desktops, tablets, mobile phones, and other emerging platforms, traditional fixed or solely responsive design approaches often fall short in addressing deeper adaptive requirements such as behavior-driven adjustments, contextual awareness, and user-specific personalization. This paper presents a hybrid model for AUI development that integrates ASP.NET MVC's robust server-side rendering pipeline with React flexible, component-based client-side architecture, enabling interfaces that not only adapt visually but also evolve functionally based on user roles, preferences, device capabilities, and real-time interaction patterns. By leveraging server-side logic for initial content shaping and client-side React components for dynamic rendering and state-driven updates, the proposed model supports fine-grained adaptation, modular UI evolution, and scalable interface personalization. Building on established concepts in responsive design, adaptive graphical interfaces, and context-aware interaction models, the study outlines key architectural strategies, design principles, and implementation techniques that facilitate the development of maintainable, high-performance AUI systems. Furthermore, the paper examines practical challenges such as context modeling, synchronization between server and client layers, managing diverse user scenarios, and optimizing rendering performance, ultimately demonstrating how the synergy of MVC and React provides a powerful foundation for creating intelligent, user-centered adaptive interfaces capable of meeting the demands of modern digital ecosystems.

detail.abstract: This study investigates how generative AI affects effort allocation in multitasking environments with asymmetric incentives. In a lab-in-the-field experiment, employees completed an incentivized writing task that could be supported by generative AI alongside a weakly incentivized calculation task that could not. Without AI, stronger incentives for writing slightly reduce calculation accuracy, consistent with classic multitasking distortions. With AI available, access improves writing quality and efficiency without reducing calculation performance. Moreover, stronger incentives for writing no longer change writing quality but generate spillovers to calculation accuracy, especially for participants without prior experience in similar writing tasks. This pattern is consistent with stronger incentives increasing reliance on AI for the primary task, compressing its cognitive demands and freeing attention for secondary work. The results inform incentive design and human-AI collaboration in AI-enabled workplaces, suggesting that firms can strengthen incentives on AI-assisted outputs without sacrificing, and sometimes improving, performance on harder-to-measure tasks.

title: Model Driven Engineering of Robust Data Pipelines: Leveraging Entity Framework Constructs with SQL Server Execution Layers

detail.title: Model Driven Engineering of Robust Data Pipelines: Leveraging Entity Framework Constructs with SQL Server Execution Layers
detail.abstract: Reliance on consistent data movement and dependable application behavior has intensified the need for pipeline architectures grounded in model driven engineering principles. The work examines how Entity Framework domain constructs can be aligned with SQL Server execution layers to create data pipelines that remain resilient, predictable, and maintainable across varied operational conditions. A mixed methodological approach is applied, combining architectural decomposition with scenario based evaluation to study how domain models, mapping configurations, query translation steps, and relational execution paths interact within a unified pipeline design. The analysis shows that pipelines structured around coherent domain abstractions exhibit clearer schema evolution pathways, reduced integration failures, and improved diagnostic transparency compared to approaches driven primarily by scripts or isolated data access logic. Integrating Entity Framework conventions with SQL Server optimization practices produces a coordinated environment in which query generation, transaction handling, and data access lifecycles operate with greater consistency. The work contributes to software engineering discourse by illustrating how model abstraction, relational processing strategy, and orchestration logic can be synthesized into a repeatable engineering method. The broader implications extend to teams responsible for transactional workloads, operational reporting platforms, and distributed application ecosystems, offering a foundation for building data pipelines that balance performance, maintainability, and long term architectural integrity.

detail.title: Airline Logistics Efficiency: KPI-Driven Strategies
detail.abstract: This study delves into the strategic significance of Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) in optimizing airline logistics and supply chain management, aiming to illuminate how these metrics drive operational efficiency, cost reduction, and enhanced customer satisfaction. Employing a mixed-methods research approach, the investigation combines quantitative analysis of airline performance data with qualitative insights from case studies and expert interviews. This comprehensive methodology facilitates a nuanced exploration of KPIs' roles across various operational dimensions, including operational efficiency, cost-effectiveness, supply chain management, and customer service quality. Findings reveal that meticulously selected and managed KPIs are pivotal in guiding strategic decision-making, fostering a data-driven culture, and achieving competitive advantage in the dynamic aviation sector. The research underscores the necessity for Chief Logistics Officers (CLOs) to implement robust KPI frameworks, integrate advanced analytics for deeper insights, and maintain agility in adapting to emerging trends and technologies. This study contributes to the academic discourse on logistics management and offers practical guidelines for airlines striving for operational excellence and strategic growth through KPI-driven strategies.

title: The Strategic Foresight of LLMs: Evidence from a Fully Prospective Venture Tournament
affiliations: University of Michigan, Stephen M. Ross School of Business,  and Indiana University Bloomington - Kelley School of Business

detail.title: The Strategic Foresight of LLMs: Evidence from a Fully Prospective Venture Tournament
detail.abstract: Can artificial intelligence outperform humans at strategic foresight—the capacity to form accurate judgments about uncertain, high-stakes outcomes before they unfold?  We address this question through a fully prospective prediction tournament using live Kickstarter crowdfunding projects.  Thirty U.S.-based technology ventures, launched after the training cutoffs of all models studied, were evaluated while fundraising remained in progress and outcomes were unknown.  A diverse suite of frontier and open-weight large language models (LLMs) completed 870 pairwise comparisons, producing complete rankings of predicted fundraising success.  We benchmarked these forecasts against 346 experienced managers recruited via Prolific and three MBA-trained investors working under monitored conditions.  The results are striking: human evaluators achieved rank correlations with actual outcomes between 0.04 and 0.45, while several frontier LLMs exceeded 0.60, with the best (Gemini 2.5 Pro) reaching 0.74—correctly ordering nearly four of every five venture pairs.  These differences persist across multiple performance metrics and robustness checks.  Neither wisdom-of-the-crowd ensembles nor human–AI hybrid teams outperformed the best standalone model.

detail.abstract:
This study evaluates how innovative banking strategies can promote financial inclusion in coastal rural communities. Financial exclusion remains a critical barrier to socioeconomic development in these areas, limiting access to credit, savings, and other essential financial services. A mixed-method approach was employed, combining case studies, literature review, and analysis of secondary data from Ghana and comparable regions to provide a comprehensive understanding of effective strategies. 
The findings indicate that ICT-based banking solutions, mobile money platforms, and strategic innovations in banking operations significantly enhance access to financial services. These interventions not only facilitate efficient financial transactions but also contribute to poverty reduction and broader community development (Annor, 2014; Joia & dos Santos, 2019; Jha, 2018). The study further highlights that tailored banking models that consider the unique socioeconomic characteristics of coastal rural communities yield higher adoption rates and long-term financial empowerment. 
The implications extend to both policymakers and banking institutions, emphasizing the need for supportive regulatory frameworks, investment in digital infrastructure, and community-focused financial literacy programs. Overall, strategic innovations in banking demonstrate substantial potential to transform financial inclusion, fostering economic resilience and sustainable development in marginalized coastal areas (Bongomin et al., 2018).

title: Misrepresentation in District-Based Elections
affiliations: , University of Michigan, Ann Arbor and Texas A&M University, College Station

detail.title: Misrepresentation in District-Based Elections
detail.abstract: State delegations are often chosen through single-member district elections, creating a tension between respecting district majorities and reflecting the statewide electorate.  First-past-the-post (FPTP) follows each district’s majority but can yield a delegation seat share far from the party’s statewide vote share. In contrast proportional representation (PR)---making a party’s seat share correspond its statewide vote share---requires departing from local majorities in some districts. We measure misrepresentation as a weighted sum of within-district misrepresentation, measured by the share of voters locally represented by their non-preferred party, and statewide misrepresentation, measured by the deviation of a party’s seat share from its statewide vote share.  The misrepresentation-minimizing rule is a cutoff rule determined by the relative weight of statewide misrepresentation. As this weight rises, the cutoff continuously shifts from FPTP’s 50% to the PR cutoff that aligns the delegation’s seat share with statewide vote shares. This shift makes gerrymandering harder, offering an alternative lever to limit gerrymandering. Using a majorization-based metric of geographic concentration, we show that concentrating support reduces misrepresentation only under the misrepresentation-minimizing rule. Within this class, FPTP and PR are uniquely characterized by the absence of cross-district spillovers and by gerrymandering-proofness, respectively. Using U.S. House elections, we infer the weights that rationalize outcomes, offering a novel metric for evaluating representativeness of district boundaries and electoral reform proposals.

title: Adam Smith and the Role of the Towns in Feudal Europe
affiliations: George Mason University - Department of Economics

detail.title: Adam Smith and the Role of the Towns in Feudal Europe
detail.abstract: Adam Smith's account of medieval towns in Book III of The Wealth of Nations remains one of the most influential analyses of how commerce transformed feudal Europe. This paper formalizes Smith's argument as a game between kings, lords, and towns. The king-town alliance emphasized by Adam Smith emerges when towns are wealthy enough to offer fiscal and military support but lords remain a credible threat. However, when kings become excessively predatory, towns may ally with lords (as in the Magna Carta crisis); when towns are too weak or too threatening, kings ally with lords instead (as in Eastern Europe or the Comuneros revolt). A dynamic extension shows that the king-town equilibrium is selfundermining: commercial growth erodes lordly military power through Smith's "diamond buckles" mechanism, eventually enabling royal absolutism. In contrast, the king-lords equilibrium is self-reinforcing, suppressing urban development and preserving feudal institutions. The framework highlights how small differences in initial urban development could generate dramatically different long-run trajectories and illuminates both the brilliance and the limitations of Smith's conjectural history.

detail.title: Affirmative Action in India with Hierarchical Reservations
detail.abstract: India implements the world's most complex affirmative action program through vertical and horizontal reservations. Although applicants can belong to at most one vertical category, they can qualify for multiple horizontal reservation categories simultaneously. We examine resource allocation problems in India, where horizontal reservations follow a hierarchical structure within a one-to-all horizontal matching framework. We introduce the hierarchical choice rule and show that it selects the most meritorious set of applicants. We thoroughly analyze the properties of the aggregate choice rule, which comprises hierarchical choice rules across all vertical categories. We show that the generalized deferred acceptance mechanism, when coupled with this aggregate choice rule, is the unique stable and strategy-proof mechanism that eliminates justified envy.

detail.abstract: Minimum Support Price (MSP) is a major agricultural policy instrument in India that affects farmer income stability, cropping decisions, and procurement planning. Reliable next-year MSP forecasting can improve decision-making for farmers, procurement agencies, and agribusiness stakeholders by supporting anticipatory planning under policy-driven price revisions. This study evaluates annual crop-wise MSP forecasting performance using official MSP data spanning 2013-14 to 2024-25 obtained from the Government of India open data portal (data.gov.in). Five models are benchmarked: Linear Regression, Polynomial Regression, Holt's Exponential Smoothing (ETS), Prophet (trend with changepoints), and Auto-ARIMA. To ensure realistic performance assessment and avoid over-optimistic in-sample metrics, models are evaluated using rolling one-step-ahead validation, simulating operational next-year prediction. Results show that Prophet achieves the best overall performance (average out-of-sample 𝑅 2 = 0.6057, RMSE=295.46) and wins for 13 crops (tied with Holt ETS). Holt ETS also performs strongly (𝑅 2 = 0.5145, RMSE=315.32) with 13 crop-wise wins. Linear Regression remains competitive (𝑅 2 = 0.5488, RMSE=315.12) but is the best model for only two crops. Auto-ARIMA underperforms substantially (average 𝑅 2 =-0.4196, RMSE=570.54), suggesting that MSP annual series are not well-described by univariate autoregressive processes. Overall, findings indicate MSP dynamics are trend-dominated with structural revisions, favoring changepointaware trend models over ARIMA-family baselines. The study concludes with implications for MSP forecasting practice and proposes policy-aware extensions incorporating inflation and input-cost indicators.

detail.abstract: This paper develops the Theory of Equal Employment Distribution (TEED) as a unified framework for addressing persistent macroeconomic challenges of low growth, inequality, and instability. Unlike conventional approaches that focus on the quantity of employment, TEED emphasizes how employment is distributed across households. When jobs are concentrated within multi-earner households while others remain jobless, aggregate demand remains structurally constrained because high-marginal-propensity-to-consume (MPC) households are excluded from the income stream. The theory demonstrates that reallocating existing employment toward high-MPC households increases aggregate consumption even when total employment, income, and the money supply remain unchanged. This redistribution generates a redistributive multiplier that raises equilibrium output and welfare without fiscal expansion, monetary easing, or inflationary pressure. Embedding the mechanism within a general equilibrium framework, the paper shows limited crowding-out effects and long-run productivity spillovers. Empirical evidence from a multi-country panel supports the theory's central predictions. The findings position employment equality as a structural engine of inclusive and non-inflationary growth.

detail.abstract: Time remains one of the most contested and foundational concepts across physics, philosophy, and the social sciences. In physics, time is treated as a dimension embedded within spacetime, shaped by gravity and velocity as described by Einstein's theories of relativity (Britannica 2025). Philosophers debate whether time exists independently of the universe or emerges from physical processes (Cycleback 2021). Cosmology suggests that time began with the Big Bang approximately 13.8 billion years ago, raising questions about whether time is finite or infinite and whether it can exist without matter or energy (Science Times 2025). This essay synthesizes these perspectives, offering mathematical formulations of time dilation, gravitational effects, and entropy. It further examines the implications of time for economic modelling, societal organization, and civilizational planning. Understanding time is essential not only for scientific inquiry but also for long-term governance, sustainability, and interplanetary exploration. The essay argues for a framework of "temporal sovereignty," in which civilizations cultivate the capacity to model, govern, and extend their temporal agency across scales of life, economy, and cosmos.

title: BERNA: Boundary-Encoded Resonance Network Architecture

detail.abstract:
Financial markets exhibit abrupt regime transitions—breaks, volatility explosions, and squeezes—that are typically identified ex post but rarely explained as necessary outcomes of an internal state law. Most existing approaches rely on price moments, efficiency ratios, or regime-duration counters, implicitly framing regime change as a detection problem rather than a mechanical consequence. As a result, price paths with similar volatility and momentum may display radically different survivability without a structural explanation.

This paper introduces BERNA (Boundary-Encoded Resonance Network Architecture), a structural failure framework in which market regimes are modeled as boundaries with finite capacity. BERNA defines three primitive state variables—accumulated structural stress (Σ), structural capacity (Θ), and remaining capacity (Λ = Θ − Σ)—that are not derived from price moments, volatility, or temporal persistence. Regime change occurs when accumulated stress exhausts capacity, formalized as a deterministic threshold event (rupture), rather than as an ex post statistical classification.

A central methodological challenge concerns reducibility to existing lifetime- or duration-based regime measures. This is addressed by demonstrating reset-invariance violation: duration counters reset by construction at regime boundaries, whereas BERNA continues to accumulate structural stress until rupture. This incompatibility precludes functional derivation or hierarchical embedding and establishes a strict direction of explanation from endogenous capacity depletion to observed regime persistence.

Empirical validation employs a broad test suite including principal component separation, permutation-based null tests, event-aligned analyses, rupture hazard modeling, structural and Markov comparisons, ablation studies, Granger causality, out-of-sample prediction, multi-asset evaluation, and robustness analyses. Across all tests, BERNA exhibits sequence-dependent behavior orthogonal to classical indicators, accumulates prior to regime failure, and remains robust to parameter and sample perturbations.

BERNA does not propose trading rules nor claim universal predictive dominance. Its contribution is diagnostic: to quantify remaining structural capacity within a regime and to explain why continuation becomes mechanically unsustainable. By replacing time-based persistence with endogenous capacity depletion, BERNA reframes regime change as a failure process rather than a detection problem.

In the empirical implementation, the capacity parameter Θ is treated as an exogenous, regime‑dependent constraint and is not inferred from price moments; a fully reproducible reference implementation is provided in Appendix A.

detail.abstract: In response to climate change, increasingly stringent emission reduction regulations require granular assessments of greenhouse gas emissions to effectively monitor and incentivize the transition toward net-zero goals. Although many companies make increasing efforts to collect emissions data for internal analyses, publicly available datasets with comparable specificity and completeness remain scarce. As a result, stakeholders, regulators, and the public are limited in their ability to apply traditional Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) methods to evaluate and guide decarbonization efforts. This study investigates alternative (LCA-based) assessment strategies that address these data limitations. We propose a hybrid framework designed to enhance the accuracy of intermediate product emission evaluations, which we validate by applying it to analyze automotive components. Informed by insights from the automotive industry, we systematically compare top-down and bottom-up, i.e. final productversus material-based, LCA methods and examine how data specificity, e.g., in production location and material composition, may affect emission estimates. Building on the findings, we introduce a hybrid LCA approach that mitigates biases inherent in the two approaches. Using a compiled multi-source database, we demonstrate the practical implementation and discuss the implications of our study for vehicle manufacturers, insurers, and repair service providers.

title: Political Pressure on the Fed - Is This Time Different?

detail.title: Political Pressure on the Fed - Is This Time Different?
detail.abstract: We examine how financial markets respond to political pressure on the Federal Reserve by US President Trump in his second term, in which his public calls for lower interest rates coincided with unprecedented efforts to reshape the Fed Board. Using a dataset of dozens of political pressure events in 2025, we use high-frequency asset price responses as multi-dimensional external instruments in a proxy VAR, identifying a political pressure shock on the Fed. We find that, unlike during Trump's first term, Fed pressure does not materialize as a de facto monetary easing: although interest rates decline, equity prices tend to fall and measures of uncertainty rise, consistent with a deterioration in market confidence. The price of gold increases particularly strongly. The identified shock can account for much of the response by financial markets to the "Liberation Day" tariff announcements in early April 2025, and continues to weigh on the USD's exchange rate, indicating a sustained loss of confidence in the dollar.

title: Engineering Global Stability: Leveraging NLP and Graph Theory to Neutralize Trade Wars

detail.title: Engineering Global Stability: Leveraging NLP and Graph Theory to Neutralize Trade Wars
detail.abstract: The global economy operates as a high-dimensional, non-linear dynamical system characterized by heterogeneous agents, asymmetric information, and non-stationary stochastic processes. Tariff impositions by major economic powers constitute exogenous shocks to complex networks of interdependent production functions, not merely bilateral price adjustments. Current retaliatory mechanisms remain fundamentally reactive, lacking predictive capacity and systemic risk awareness. Drawing from rigorous training in infectious disease modeling, social network dynamics, and computational epidemiology, I formalize Algorithmic Reciprocity: a data-driven system engineered to detect, model, and neutralize economic contagion before cascading systemic failures propagate through global trade networks. This framework integrates spectral graph theory, temporal network analysis, adversarial machine learning, and cryptoeconomic mechanism design to deliver: 1. The Ripple Engine — Temporal graph neural network for multi-hop economic shock propagation 2. Mirror — Adversarial verification layer combining distributed data fusion with causal inference 3. Trust Coefficient Framework — Bayesian reputation system with incentive-compatible disclosure mechanisms 4. Shield Protocol — Automated redistribution via smart contracts with Byzantine fault tolerance.

title: Why the Environment Plays a Major Role in Everything: An Economist’s Perspective

detail.title: Why the Environment Plays a Major Role in Everything: An Economist’s Perspective
detail.abstract: The environment is the primary source of raw materials that sustain economic activity and form the foundation of production. From an economist's perspective, natural resources-such as land, minerals, water, forests, and energy-are essential inputs for the factors of production: land, labour, capital, and entrepreneurship (Tietenberg & Lewis, 2018). This paper examines how the availability and quality of raw materials influence production costs, product prices, and consumer purchasing power, highlighting the broader macroeconomic consequences of environmental degradation and resource depletion (Dasgupta, 2001). It also discusses the economic rationale for safeguarding natural resources through efficient management, government regulation, market-based instruments, technological innovation, and sustainable consumption practices (Pearce et al., 2013). The study demonstrates that sustainable resource management is critical not only for environmental protection but also for maintaining economic efficiency, stability, and long-term growth (Stiglitz, 2019). By linking environmental conditions to production, market dynamics, and policy measures, the paper emphasizes why the environment plays a major role in everything from an economist's viewpoint.

title: The Jevons Filter: Why Civilizations May Fail Before Reaching Type I Status

detail.title: The Jevons Filter: Why Civilizations May Fail Before Reaching Type I Status

declarations.declarationOfInterest: no

detail.abstract: Humanity's accelerating energy use poses profound questions about the long-term viability of technological civilization. This paper introduces the "Jevons Filter" hypothesis: a selfreinforcing feedback loop between efficiency improvements and rising aggregate consumption, rooted in the classical Jevons Paradox that systematically drives civilizations toward resource depletion and environmental thresholds. Drawing on economic history, thermodynamic modeling, and astrobiology, we argue that this feedback constitutes a critical developmental barrier, hindering sustainable progression toward Kardashev Type I energy mastery. By amplifying the risks of overshoot, the Jevons Filter may form part of the Great Filter proposed to account for the Fermi Paradox. We develop a simplified thermodynamic model linking energy efficiency, economic expansion, and civilizational dynamics, and critically engage with counterarguments regarding absolute decoupling and transformative technological innovations. Our analysis suggests that without fundamental structural transformations to break the growthconsumption cycle, civilizations are likely to face collapse or stagnation before reaching stable, planetary-scale energy management. Grasping this embedded dynamic is essential for futures thinking: overcoming the Jevons Filter may represent an exceptionally rare and difficult pathway, requiring sweeping reorientations in socioeconomic priorities, governance frameworks, and cultural values. This paper emphasizes the implications for sustainability transitions and reframes planetary stewardship as a central determinant of civilizational longevity.

detail.abstract: Indonesia is the world's largest archipelagic state, characterized by a high degree of geographical, demographic, and cultural diversity, encompassing hundreds of ethnic groups, rich cultural traditions and customary practices, a wide range of local languages, and abundant natural resources. This diversity constitutes both a national asset and a challenge in maintaining the unity and integrity of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia (NKRI). detail.abstract: Modern economics measures value primarily through monetary indicators—prices, capital, credit, and market expectations. Human time, however, remains only indirectly quantified via wages, labor costs, discounting, or productivity metrics derived from money. This paper proposes treating human time as a non-monetary economic primitive: a primary accounting unit of productivity that is not reducible to money and does not depend on debt-based issuance. We introduce a formal research framework in which time can function as an accounting dimension, parallel to monetary systems, without claiming to replace them. The paper defines core concepts, invariants, non-goals, and verification requirements for a spec-first architecture suitable for independent critique and simulation. The result is not a product or deployable protocol, but a research scaffold for examining whether a value layer based on human time can exist without becoming a currency or investment instrument.

detail.abstract: Olive oil is one of the most important products in the Spanish agri-food sector, with Spain accounting for 50 percent of world production. Despite Spain’s leadership in global olive oil production, the sector faces significant challenges in commercialization, both domestically and abroad. This highlights the need to implement more effective international marketing strategies. This article therefore focuses on analysing the key internationalization actions of the Spanish olive oil industry. To that end, the Qualitative Comparative Analysis (QCA) method is used, applying the fuzzy set approach (fsQCA). The results show that for companies in the sector to internationalize they must: (1) have objective knowledge of the market and experience of other internationalization processes; (2) create international networks through relationships with prescribers, chefs and commercial distributors; (3) the founder must be innovative, proactive, proactive, have the autonomy and competitive aggressiveness to offer innovative products, and have commercial units abroad. detail.abstract: This paper provides a critical analysis of Republic Act No. 11058, signed on August 17, 2018, transitioned occupational safety and health to a required legislative requirement in the Philippines. The law seeks to shield employees from hazardous situations by mandating companies to provide a hazard-free workplace and free personal protective equipment (PPE). RA 11058 gives workers the right to know the potential risks and hazards at work and the right to decline work in a hazardous situation without fear of retaliation. Additionally, for compliance, the law mandates the appointment of safety officers and a fine of ₱100,000 for every day a violation remains uncorrected. Although its effectiveness is hindered by the double standard created by the exclusion of the public sector. Its one-size-fits-all penalty system also poses a significant burden on the financial stance of MSMEs. Overall, RA 11058 is a vital social law that protects employees, it would be further effective if the law were amended to include the public sector and to provide specialized training and support systems for MSMEs.

detail.abstract: Mountain tourism in Nepal has expanded rapidly, particularly in the Annapurna region, raising concerns about environmental pressure and the sustainability of trekking practices. While trekkers' experience has often been linked to satisfaction and pro-environmental behaviour, empirical evidence from Himalayan contexts remains limited. This study investigates the relationship between trekkers' experience, satisfaction, and sustainable behaviour, and examines the role of guiding practices within the framework of Nepal's trekking policies. A quantitative survey was conducted with 400 international trekkers in the Annapurna region. Descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, and regression models were applied to examine relationships between experience dimensions, satisfaction, and self-reported sustainable behaviour. The study contributes to debates on sustainable mountain tourism by highlighting the importance of experience quality and governance mechanisms rather than satisfaction alone in shaping responsible behaviour. Policy implications are discussed in relation to guiding regulation, visitor management, and sustainability in high-altitude destinations.
