title: Blockchain and the Future of Stock Trading Infrastructure: Clearing, Settlement, and Regulatory Oversight

detail.title: Blockchain and the Future of Stock Trading Infrastructure: Clearing, Settlement, and Regulatory Oversight
detail.abstract: This paper explores the structural transformation of capital markets through the integration of Distributed Ledger Technology (DLT) and blockchain. While current market infrastructures rely on fragmented, siloed databases requiring costly reconciliation (T+1), blockchain offers a unified, immutable "Golden Record" capable of atomic (T+0) settlement. We analyze practical applications across the Front, Middle, and Back Office, evaluate global case studies (Switzerland's SDX, Australia's ASX), and propose a technical architecture using permissioned ledgers (Corda/Hyperledger). Finally, we present a strategic roadmap for financial institutions to transition from legacy systems to tokenized ecosystems, addressing regulatory compliance (SEC, CFTC) and operational risk.It is trying to examine application of blockchain technology across the full stock trading lifecycle. Modern equity markets operate through highly complex institutional arrangements involving exchanges, broker-dealers, clearing members, central counterparties, custodians, asset servicers, and regulators. Despite decades of automation, many post-trade processes remain reconciliation-driven, fragmented, and operationally expensive. Blockchain-based distributed ledger technology introduces a synchronized, immutable record of transactions shared among authorized participants. From a financial market infrastructure perspective, this shared-state model materially reduces settlement risk, operational latency, and data inconsistency.

title: Dynamic Compensation, Market Rotation and Fairness Concern
affiliations: The University of Hong Kong, University of Texas at Dallas - Naveen Jindal School of Management, The University of Hong Kong - Faculty of Business and Economics and Zhejiang University

detail.title: Dynamic Compensation, Market Rotation and Fairness Concern
detail.abstract: Problem definition: Sales territory management often faces a fundamental conflict between incentivizing agents and maintaining workforce equity, a tension driven by structural market heterogeneity where territories differ significantly in revenue potential and effort costs. While firms increasingly internalize fairness concerns to provide a better working environment, compensating disadvantaged agents with monetary premiums can be prohibitively expensive. Methodology/results: We investigate this trade-off using a dynamic principal-agent model to determine the optimal joint design of compensation and territory rotation. We characterize the optimal contract and demonstrate that, contrary to the intuition that rotation is a simple wealth-sharing mechanism, the optimal policy employs conditional rotation triggered by agent failure under certain market conditions. This mechanism leverages the territory as a disciplinary device, which imposes a credible "threat of demotion" and "path to promotion" to substitute for monetary fairness premiums. We find that a rigid pursuit of fairness without operational flexibility may backfire, forcing the firm to reduce job security to manage inflated costs. In contrast, optimal rotation can yield a strict Pareto improvement under certain market conditions and cost structures, simultaneously increasing firm profits, agent compensation, and workforce retention. Finally, we extend our framework to include costly rotation, deriving a strict economic boundary where rotation is viable and beneficial. Managerial implications: Our results warn managers against relying solely on wage compression to address equity and instead advocate for a performance-contingent rotation strategy that effectively balances the cost of inequality against the cost of intervention.

title: Rethinking Optimal Decumulation: A New Value-Function Formulation within the HJB Framework

detail.title: Rethinking Optimal Decumulation: A New Value-Function Formulation within the HJB Framework
detail.abstract: In this research, we develop a novel decumulation framework for retirement portfolios designed to preserve stable withdrawals while dynamically adapting investment risk. Traditional approaches to decumulation fall into two main paradigms: utility-based models, which co-optimize consumption and asset allocation but yield volatile income, and constant-coupon strategies, which enforce spending stability but rely on static or rule-based allocations. Our contribution lies in reconciling these paradigms by retaining a fixed coupon and formulating a state-contingent allocation policy within the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman framework. The model introduces a new value function based on relative (consumption-adjusted) wealth to ensure economically interpretable behavior: underfunded states induce higher risk-taking to restore sustainability, while overfunded states trigger de-risking. The allocation rule thus adapts naturally to funding status without sacrificing income stability. We validate the framework through extensive simulations under Gaussian and heavy-tailed dynamics, as well as real-world asset classes. Results demonstrate that, at moderate payout levels (4%), the model achieves near-complete survival probabilities while avoiding excessive bequests. At higher payouts (6%), survival rates remain materially higher than those of constant-mix or glidepath benchmarks, confirming robustness to sequence-of-returns risk. Real-data applications corroborate these findings, showing realistic allocation patterns and strong sustainability. The framework advances the decumulation literature by combining the tractability of stochastic control with the practical appeal of constant withdrawals, offering a robust methodology that dynamically aligns risk with the current funding status.

title: Impact of Leverages on Profitability of Select High and Low Performing Sugar Companies in India
affiliations: Sri Krishna Adithya College of Arts & Science and PSG College of Arts and Science

detail.title: Impact of Leverages on Profitability of Select High and Low Performing Sugar Companies in India

publicationDetails.detailsText: OIDA International Journal of Sustainable Development, 19 (02), 151-166, 2026.
publicationDetails.journalName: OIDA International Journal of Sustainable Development

detail.abstract: The sugar industry in India has been immensely beneficial in promoting the economy of some of the nearby countryside, agricultural-industrial jobs, and regional infrastructure development, mainly in sugar-growing states such as Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, and Tamil Nadu. Nevertheless, the increasing financial disparity between well-performing and underperforming sugar companies is exacerbating uneven regional growth, poor infrastructure utilization, and economic stagnation in rural areas. The ineffective use of financial and operating leverage, which influences the profitability and, therefore, the ability of the firms to reinvest in the local communities and economic planning, is one of the major underlying causes of such imbalance. These issues have direct tensions on the goal of SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth), SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure), and SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities), particularly within economically fragile regions. This paper presents an organised financial analysis of some of the top and low-performing sugar firms in India between the years 2019 and 2024. It is a financial ratio analysis and the regression model-based analysis that assesses the impact that leverage decisions, as quantified by Return on Assets (ROA), Net Profit Margin (NPM), and Earnings Per Share (EPS) data have on profitability and consequently regional contributions. The results indicate that firms with an effectively balanced leverage structure are not only more profitable but also tend to foster local community development, drive infrastructural growth, and exhibit greater resilience in employment creation. On the contrary, those companies with poorly balanced leverage do not contribute to the regional economic development, worsening the spatial inequality. The research findings indicate that the exploitation of industrial sectors such as sugar should be incorporated in regional development plans, which ought to be sustainable and fair in development over time. This contributes to the achievement of SDGs 8, 9, and 11 of regional sustainable planning.

title: The US Treasury Funding Advantage Since 1860
affiliations: , ,  and Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System

detail.title: The US Treasury Funding Advantage Since 1860
detail.abstract: We provide the first consistent historical estimate of US Treasury funding advantage, as measured by term structures of yield spreads between comparable highest-grade US corporate bonds and Treasurys. We construct a new dataset with monthly prices, cash-flows, and ratings for US corporate bonds over 1860-2024. We adjust yield curve estimation techniques to account for tax treatments and embedded options. Existing index-based spreads have mismeasured US funding advantage on long-term bonds in the post-WWI period, particularly during high inflation episodes. An asset pricing model for US funding advantage finds that standard risk factors, not quantity changes, explain most variation in spreads.

title: Explainable Patterns in Cryptocurrency Microstructure
affiliations: University of Warsaw, Faculty of Economic Sciences and University of Warsaw - Faculty of Economic Sciences

detail.title: Explainable Patterns in Cryptocurrency Microstructure
detail.abstract: We document stable cross-asset patterns in cryptocurrency limit-order-book microstructure: the same engineered order book and trade features exhibit remarkably similar predictive importance and SHAP dependence shapes across assets spanning an order of magnitude in market capitalization (BTC, LTC, ETC, ENJ, ROSE). The data covers Binance Futures perpetual contract order books and trades on 1-second frequency starting from January 1st, 2022 up to October 12th, 2025. Using a unified CatBoost modeling pipeline with a direction-aware GMADL objective and time-series cross validation, we show that feature rankings and partial effects are stable across assets despite heterogeneous liquidity and volatility. We connect these SHAP structures to microstructure theory (order flow imbalance, spread, and adverse selection) and validate tradability via a conservative top-of-book taker backtest as well as fixed depth maker backtest. Our primary novelty is a robustness analysis of a major flash crash, where the divergent performance of our taker and maker strategies empirically validates classic microstructure theories of adverse selection and highlights the systemic risks of algorithmic trading. Our results suggest a portable microstructure representation of short-horizon returns and motivate universal feature libraries for crypto markets.

title: Corporate Democratic Responsibility: The Role of Companies in Supporting Democracy

detail.title: Corporate Democratic Responsibility: The Role of Companies in Supporting Democracy
detail.abstract: This article introduces the concept of Corporate Democratic Responsibility (CDR) and its practical application through Corporate Democratic Education (CDE), exploring how businesses can actively contribute to safeguarding the integrity and stability of democratic societies. As democracy faces increasing challenges-such as political disengagement, disinformation, populism, and the erosion of democratic norms-companies are expected not only to avoid undermining democracy but also to contribute proactively to its preservation. Building on Böckenförde's reflections on the preconditions of democracy and Popper's defense of the open society, CDR extends the traditional scope of Corporate Social Responsibility and Political Corporate Social Responsibility, urging companies to take purposeful roles in strengthening democratic institutions. CDE operationalizes this by promoting political literacy and fostering civic engagement among both internal and external stakeholders, ensuring that businesses play a pivotal role in cultivating a more informed and resilient citizenry. The paper concludes with a call for future research on the implications of CDR and CDE for CSR and the evolving role of businesses in shaping public discourse in democracies. Given the increasing threats to democratic systems, deepening our understanding of these concepts is crucial for both academic inquiry and guiding business practices, helping organizations contribute to democracy's resilience.

title: U.S.-China Chip War: Export Controls, EUV Lithography, ASML, and China's "Manhattan Project"

detail.title: U.S.-China Chip War: Export Controls, EUV Lithography, ASML, and China's "Manhattan Project"
detail.abstract:
This article argues that the United States–China chip war has evolved from industrial rivalry into a structural contest over the infrastructure of twenty-first-century power. At the center lies the ability to design and manufacture frontier logic semiconductors—especially through extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography—now a material precondition for artificial intelligence (AI), high-performance computing, and next-generation military systems. Building on the framework of “weaponized interdependence,” the paper maps how U.S. export controls—via the Bureau of Industry and Security Entity List, the Foreign Direct Product Rule (FDPR), and “U.S. persons” restrictions—operate as coercive governance of chokepoints across an asymmetric global ecosystem, including EDA software, manufacturing equipment, and technical services.

The paper’s central finding is paradoxical but policy-critical: export controls can raise costs, slow “time-to-iterate,” and degrade yields—yet they also intensify China’s incentives for substitution, indigenization, and whole-of-state mobilization, potentially accelerating long-run sanction resilience. It then examines the strategic role of ASML’s EUV monopoly as a geopolitical chokepoint, and assesses open-source reporting on China’s Shenzhen “Manhattan Project” and alternative technological pathways (including accelerator-based EUV concepts) as routes to bypass interdiction. Crucially, the analysis shifts the spotlight from hardware to “human transfer”: covert talent recruitment, identity shielding, and pragmatic manipulation of nationality and residency rules as mechanisms to move tacit know-how that export controls struggle to regulate.

The article concludes that the most plausible medium-term outcome is technological bifurcation—two partially autonomous semiconductor universes—while warning that coercive “windows of vulnerability” can compress crisis timelines and raise miscalculation risks. It proposes a portfolio strategy that pairs calibrated controls with affirmative capacity-building and legally constrained research-security governance to avoid self-defeating overbreadth.

title: Imagining Indigenous Islamic Financial Modernity: What If Colonialism Never Disrupted Islamic Banking?

detail.title: Imagining Indigenous Islamic Financial Modernity: What If Colonialism Never Disrupted Islamic Banking?
detail.abstract: Contemporary Islamic finance operates predominantly through retrofitting Western financial architecture with Shariah-compliant modifications. This paper poses a counter-factual question: what institutional forms might have emerged had indigenous Islamic financial evolution continued uninterrupted from the Abbasid era through Ottoman modernity? Drawing on Udovitch's (1970) analysis of medieval Islamic partnerships, Çizakça's (2011) work on Ottoman financial innovations, and Goitein's (1967-1993) Geniza scholarship, this study traces the sophisticated trajectory of pre-colonial Islamic financial institutions-including mudaraba partnerships, suftaja networks, cash waqf systems, and esham securities-before their systematic displacement through colonial intervention. The analysis reveals that nineteenth-century disruption foreclosed genuinely alternative developmental pathways, leaving contemporary Islamic finance to reconstruct from fragments what might have constituted a coherent indigenous financial architecture. This counterfactual framework illuminates both the contingency of current arrangements and potential design spaces for authentic Islamic financial innovation.

title: The Dimensional Structure of Welfare in Heterogeneous-Firm General Equilibrium *
affiliations: Shanhai Academy of Social Science, Shanhai Academy of Social Science

detail.title: The Dimensional Structure of Welfare in Heterogeneous-Firm General Equilibrium *
detail.abstract: This paper clarifies the dimensional structure of welfare in heterogeneous-firm general equilibrium and develops a tractable sufficient-statistics framework. Despite the high-dimensional nature of Melitz-type models, we show that welfare depends on only two orthogonal margins: the extensive margin of product varieties and the selection margin of the productivity cutoff. The one-dimensional welfare formula commonly used in the literature arises only when the measure of varieties is fixed. Relaxing this restriction yields a two-dimensional representation that remains valid in multi-country and multi-sector environments and provides a transparent dimensional reduction. We further show how an additional knowledge margin can incorporate export-learning effects into welfare analysis. The result is a unified and flexible toolkit for generalequilibrium counterfactuals.

title: The Shift from Traditional Pensions to 401(k)s: Retirement Risks and the Timing of Retirement
affiliations: Rutgers University, New Brunswick - Department of Economics,  and Louisiana State University Shreveport

detail.title: The Shift from Traditional Pensions to 401(k)s: Retirement Risks and the Timing of Retirement
detail.abstract: U.S. retirement plans have shifted sharply from defined benefit to defined contribution setups. How has this change affected retirement and savings behavior? We develop a quantitative life-cycle model where retirement plans differ in their exposure to longevity and investment risk. Holding the present-value cost of benefits fixed, these differences generate distinct savings and retirement incentives across plan types. The model replicates observed differences in savings and retirement behavior and implies that the shift from defined benefit to defined contribution plans alone accounts for roughly 92% of the decline in retirement by age 65 since the early 1990s. We then consider a policy that allows retirees to convert accumulated assets into actuarially fair annuities. Access to annuitization increases welfare and induces earlier retirement, with substantially larger effects in an economy that relies more heavily on defined contribution plans.

title:
A Home Run for Cobb? 
A Comprehensive Report on the Economic Impact of Truist Park and The Battery Atlanta on Cobb County

detail.title:
A Home Run for Cobb? 
A Comprehensive Report on the Economic Impact of Truist Park and The Battery Atlanta on Cobb County

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author has no conflicts of interest to report.
declarations.funderStatement: The author is a faculty affiliate of the Bagwell Center for the Study of Markets and Economic Opportunity at Kennesaw State University, and he received summer research support from this organization in 2020, while conducting related research. The author is solely responsible for the content in this report and had complete academic freedom to conduct his research.

publicationDetails.detailsText: This Policy Report was originally published by the Bagwell Center for the Study of Markets and Economic Opportunity at Kennesaw State University. I am posting it here to ensure a stable link.

detail.abstract:
This report provides a comprehensive retrospective assessment of the Atlanta Braves' Truist Park development using publicly-available data and standard empirical methods to estimate its economic effects on Cobb County. The key findings are: 

 - Sales tax revenue increased following the stadium’s opening; however, much of the spending associated with the stadium development appears to have come at the expense of existing Cobb businesses; thus, net gains to commercial activity have been small. 

 - Cobb property value growth, near the stadium and countywide, has been typical for the Atlanta region, which does not reflect net positive economic or social benefits from the stadium, nor has the stadium’s presence expanded the County’s budget through increased property tax assessments. 

 - Stadium-induced tax revenue has fallen well short of covering Cobb’s public investment in the stadium, costing taxpayers nearly $15 million per year to service stadium debt and fund operations, which translates to approximately $50 per Cobb household. 

Overall, Cobb’s experience with Truist Park has been similar to most other stadium projects, which fail to generate large economic benefits to host communities.

title: "Stationary Valuation and Price-Quantity Dynamics in Non-Equilibrium Economies"
affiliations: The Association of Chartered Certified Accountants (ACCA)

detail.title: "Stationary Valuation and Price-Quantity Dynamics in Non-Equilibrium Economies"
detail.abstract: This paper develops a non-equilibrium framework linking price and quantity dynamics through a stationarity condition on cumulative value expenditure under bounded coordination. Prices are interpreted as dynamic value flows-the temporal realization of quantities-rather than as equilibrium-clearing signals. Stationarity implies an inverse unit valuation and a lower bound on joint price-quantity dispersion, constraining admissible adjustment paths in non-equilibrium economies. Within this framework, asset price peaks correspond to turning points in growth dynamics rather than equilibrium outcomes or market collapses. The analysis reveals a structural trade-off between price coordination and quantity adjustment, generating endogenous instability without reliance on behavioral biases, equilibrium breakdowns, or exogenous shocks. The results contribute to non-equilibrium political economy by clarifying intrinsic limits to price-based coordination in complex economic systems and offering a unified interpretation of bubbles and market fragility.

title: How Wars Create Winners and Losers in the Global Economy
affiliations: Kiel Institute for the World Economy

detail.title: How Wars Create Winners and Losers in the Global Economy
detail.abstract: Wars create winners and losers in the global economy. Using data on 49 interstate wars from 1962-2023, I trace spillovers to third countries via the terms of trade. When warring countries are dominant suppliers of specific products, global market prices of these products rise. Third countries importing these products suffer lower output and higher inflation, while countries exporting these products boom. A 1-standard-deviation war shock on the export basket lifts output by 1 percent. The same shock on import baskets reduces output by 2 percent. The results exist over and above direct trade channels and extend beyond energy-supply shocks.

title: Replicating Political Economy Weights in Ossa (2014): An Optimization-based Alternative

detail.title: Replicating Political Economy Weights in Ossa (2014): An Optimization-based Alternative
detail.abstract: We replicate the political economy weights in Ossa (2014) using a Levenberg-Marquardt optimization framework. The optimization routine yields clearer firstorder optimality diagnostics, with Japan showing the most notable differences relative to the heuristic procedure, while most other countries display outcomes that are numerically close to the original implementation. Despite these differences in the underlying weights, the implied optimal tariff profiles remain highly stable across methods.

title: What's In a Name? What Exactly Does One Mean, When One Says 'Merger' [In EU Merger Regulation]?

detail.title: What's In a Name? What Exactly Does One Mean, When One Says 'Merger' [In EU Merger Regulation]?
detail.abstract: EU Merger Regulation (EUMR) deals with concentrations with a community dimension. What are the criteria to determine whether a given transaction qualifies as a concentration with a community dimension? Are concentrations the same as mergers, or is concentration a broader term that may include transactions, in addition to mergers? Do acquisitions, and joint ventures, for example, qualify as concentrations, that are different from mergers? From an inter-disciplinary lens, is the meaning of merger same or is it different from the notion as understood in different disciplines, such as in the corporate finance literature? What are the criteria to qualify a transaction as a merger? This contribution deliberates on the foregoing considerations.

title: Loanly Governments
affiliations: Universidad Carlos III de Madrid and

detail.title: Loanly Governments
detail.abstract: We compile a new dataset on government liabilities by instrument for 33 advanced economies and document that a substantial share of government debt consists of loans rather than bonds. To study governments' loan-bond portfolio choice, we exploit high-frequency variation in bond yields around sovereign credit rating announcements. Our analysis yields three main findings. First, increasing bond yields cause the government to substitute from bond to loan-based borrowing. Second, this substitution is mirrored by foreign creditors, who reduce their direct bond holdings and increasingly provide funding indirectly through domestic bank loans. Third, this shift toward domestic bank loans is associated with elevated levels of financial distress. Finally, we discuss how these findings can be rationalized when repatriating government debt through domestic banks reduces sovereign default risk. This mitigates the initial bond yield increase, albeit at the expense of higher bank balance sheet risk.

title: Dealers as Record Keepers
affiliations: The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK) - CUHK Business School and HEC Paris - Finance Department

detail.title: Dealers as Record Keepers
detail.abstract: Trading relationships in over-the-counter (OTC) markets are persistent and often exclusive, despite technological advances that have expanded clients' access to dealers. We rationalize this pattern in a model where trading relationships allow dealers to learn their clients' trading motives from their trading records. Relationship dealers set record-contingent quotes, generating price discrimination that mitigates adverse selection for liquidity-driven clients. Moreover, we show that clients prefer exclusive relationships to keep their record private. As a result, post-trade transparency and trading protocols that facilitate public inference of clients' trading records by dealers (e.g., Request for Quote relative to Request for Market) may reduce gains from trade.

title: Broadband Internet and Fact-Resistant Beliefs: The Case of Climate Change Skepticism

detail.title: Broadband Internet and Fact-Resistant Beliefs: The Case of Climate Change Skepticism
detail.abstract: In the present study, I explore the informational role of broadband internet in forming and spreading fact-resistant attitudes, specifically climate change skepticism. My approach uses fine-grained broadband quality data in the U.S. along with an identification strategy relying on terrain-induced variations in the cost of broadband deployment. Overall, the results indicate that better internet can encourage unwarranted skepticism, albeit only to a limited extent. Suggestive evidence is further consistent with middle-aged and more Republican-leaning segments of the population driving any negative overall impacts toward denialism, while younger and less conservative segments, if at all, tend to respond in the opposite way.

title: Internalizing the Negative Externality from Urbanization: Evidence from India’s Rurban Mission
affiliations: Indian Institute of Management Calcutta,  and Indian Institute of Management Calcutta

detail.title: Internalizing the Negative Externality from Urbanization: Evidence from India’s Rurban Mission
detail.abstract: Can an urbanization push generate economic gains while mitigating its associated environmental costs? We study a unique place-based policy in India, the Rurban Mission, launched in 2016, that created 300 “rurban” clusters of contiguous villages, with the objective of extending the agglomeration benefits of urbanization, while explicitly emphasizing the preservation of rural institutions at its core. Exploiting the staggered rollout of the policy, and drawing on satellite data on nighttime lights and PM2.5, we implement a synthetic difference-in-differences design. We find that the program increased regional economic activity while modestly reducing air pollution, with stronger environmental gains in tribal clusters where local institutions reinforced sustainability objectives. Our findings indicate that place-based policies that leverage the existing institutional setup of rural settings can achieve the economic gains from urbanization with minimal environmental costs.

title: Concealed Third-Party Litigation Funding
affiliations: Bar Ilan University School of Law

detail.title: Concealed Third-Party Litigation Funding

publicationDetails.detailsText: Theoretical Inquiries in Law, volume 25, issue 2, 2024[10.1515/til-2024-0024 ]

detail.abstract: Litigation entails substantial expenses, such as attorney fees and payment to experts. Third-party litigation funding aids individuals and enterprises who lack the financial means to pursue legal action by providing financial support to cover these expenses in return for a portion of the gains. The current literature focuses on direct, for-profit funding. This Article extends the discussion to other funding opportunities. Among these, concealed litigation funding alludes to a scenario where a funder's investment decreases the costs for one of the litigants, but without any direct transfer of funds. In return, the funder acquires an indirect advantage, such as reducing its own liability risk or the liability risk of its investors. Several jurisdictions restrict direct funding, citing concerns about increased litigation, decreasing incentives to settle, and interference with litigants' case management. This Article highlights the potential consequences of regulating only direct, for-profit funding. It suggests that other forms of funding, such as donations or concealed funding, distort litigation incentives more than direct funding. As a result, restricting direct funding harms litigants who do not have access to concealed funding without solving the problems of excessive litigation and unwillingness to settle.

title: Brightening the Night Sky: The Contribution of Soybean Imports to China's Urbanization
affiliations: Ningbo University, Huazhong University of Science and Technology and Huazhong University of Science and Technology

detail.title: Brightening the Night Sky: The Contribution of Soybean Imports to China's Urbanization

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.

detail.abstract: This study exploits China's removal of the tariff rate quota on imported soybeans (TRQS) in 1999 as a quasi-natural experiment to examine the role of soybean imports in promoting urbanization. Using a generalized difference-indifferences strategy, it investigates the policy's heterogeneous effects on nighttime light intensity across cities at varying distances from the shortest coastline. The results show that cities located closer to the coastline experienced significantly larger increases in nighttime light intensity. Moreover, manufacturing enterprises in these areas exhibited greater employment growth, particularly within nonknowledge-intensive manufacturing sectors. According to our conservative estimates, the removal of the TRQS accounted for approximately 12% of the growth in nighttime light intensity. This study identifies four mechanisms through which soybean imports promoted China's urbanization: (1) substituting for domestic oil crop production; (2) meeting the rapidly rising urban demand for edible oil and high-protein foods; (3) encouraging agricultural scale expansion and mechanization, thereby advancing labor-saving technologies and raising agricultural productivity; and (4) conserving agricultural land while facilitating the expansion of urban construction land.

title:
Agriculture, Finance, and Sustainability 
Emerging Challenges and Future Pathways 
Agriculture, Finance, and Sustainability: Emerging Challenges and Future Pathways
affiliations: Centurion University of Technology and Management, Paralakhemundi, Odisha, India and Symbiosis University of Applied Sciences, Indore

detail.title:
Agriculture, Finance, and Sustainability 
Emerging Challenges and Future Pathways 
Agriculture, Finance, and Sustainability: Emerging Challenges and Future Pathways
detail.abstract: This book targets a wide range of readers: researchers and postgraduates who need to find combined principles; policymakers that need to create agricultural and financial solutions that can withstand climate change; practitioners in the spheres of banking, insurance, and technological finance; and people employed in agribusiness and value chains as well as technology platforms. We want to get the gap between conceptualization and practical evidence and policy relevance- providing a consistent perspective of how finance, technology, governance, and sustainability can be mutually defining in the creation of resilient agricultural futures. We also hope the book leads readers beyond siloed solutions into the realm of system thinking in which climate adaptation, financial inclusion, productivity growth and environmental stewardship are all addressed in a concerted effort through a co-ordinated design. The rest of the restraints is upon us, and we can embrace further academic work and practitioner consultation to make this developing discipline robust.

title: Measuring Policy Tone in FOMC Statements with GraphRAG Fine-Tuning
affiliations: ,  and Hankuk University of Foreign Studies

detail.title: Measuring Policy Tone in FOMC Statements with GraphRAG Fine-Tuning
detail.abstract:
The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) post-meeting statement conveys assessments of policy and macro-financial conditions, and its tone can shape market expectations and financial volatility. Moving beyond lexicon-based, reduced-form textual, and standalone large language model (LLM) approaches, this paper proposes a Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation (GraphRAG)-based framework that extends the view of policy tone as a signal by embedding macroeconomic theory and institutional policy information into the interpretation of FOMC statements. The resulting sentiment measure is designed to be stable, interpretable, and context aware. 

Empirically, policy-tone sentiment is shown to be state dependent. Its correlation with inflation changes markedly across pre-and post-pandemic regimes, while the sentiment signal is most informative for financial conditions as measured by NFCI (National Financial Conditions Index) and ANFCI, which remove inflation-driven variation. In rolling-window ARX and ARIMAX forecasts, the GraphRAG specification incorporating theoretical and policy context consistently achieves the lowest prediction errors, indicating superior macro-financial predictive content.

title: The Geometric Bird and the Traveling Gaze: Paolo Uccello Seen by Chinese Tourists and Western Art History

detail.title: The Geometric Bird and the Traveling Gaze: Paolo Uccello Seen by Chinese Tourists and Western Art History
detail.abstract: This article examines the paintings of Paolo Uccello through a comparative perspective that contrasts Western art-historical interpretation with the ways in which contemporary Chinese tourists encounter and perceive his works in European museums. Rather than treating linear perspective as a universal achievement or normative standard of visual rationality, the study analyses how different cultural traditions of seeing shape the attribution of meaning to Uccello's geometry, stylization, and artificiality. Drawing on observations of museum practices, digital travel media, and visual commentary, the article shows that Chinese viewers often approach Uccello outside the teleological framework of Renaissance progress that dominates Western scholarship. Elements frequently regarded in Western discourse as deficiencies-rigidity, decorative excess, emotional distance-are instead perceived as deliberate construction and aesthetic choice. Perspective appears not primarily as a scientific breakthrough but as a visible system of ordering space. By juxtaposing these modes of reception, the article argues that Uccello's work functions as a productive site for cross-cultural reflection on vision, realism, and pictorial logic. The analysis contributes to broader debates on global museum audiences, the cultural contingency of art-historical categories, and the shifting meanings of canonical European art in a transnational context.

title: Twenty Laws in Schumpeterian Economics
affiliations: University of Zaragoza and University of Zaragoza

detail.title: Twenty Laws in Schumpeterian Economics
detail.abstract: Since the foundation of the International Schumpeter Society (ISS) in 1986, the fields of economics of innovation, innovation studies more broadly, evolutionary Schumpeterian economics, and the analysis of economies as evolving complex systems have made tremendous progress. Furthermore, around the ISS and connected authors, a new paradigm in economic thought has emerged. This paradigm provides new insights which have been tested, applied and are currently in diffusion throughout significant parts of the economics and business communities. With occasion of the 40 th anniversary of the ISS, the time is ripe for Schumpeterian economists to take stock and put forward neatly the results of the new paradigm. In this chapter, we have selected twenty laws in Schumpeterian economics as a sample of this body of works. These laws enrich the landscape of economic thinking in the 21 st century and may engage new scholars and practitioners interested in the field. An agenda for the future is also outlined.

title: Attributed Belief Equilibrium: Psychological Games between Humans and AI

detail.title: Attributed Belief Equilibrium: Psychological Games between Humans and AI
detail.abstract: We introduce Attributed Belief Equilibrium (ABE) to analyse strategic interaction between humans and artificial agents. In these games, humans have belief-dependent preferences-guilt, anger, or reciprocity-while AI have design-dependent objectives. Humans systematically attribute mental states to AI through anthropomorphism, forming attributed beliefs about what AI expect. These attributed beliefs enter human utility through standard psychological mechanisms but satisfy different consistency conditions than genuine beliefs. We establish existence under regularity conditions, show that different attribution patterns sustain different equilibria, and derive welfare implications for AI design. Elevated anthropomorphism improves welfare with prosocial AI but reduces welfare with materialistic AI. The framework provides foundations for analysing cooperation, trust, and coordination in mixed human-AI populations.

title: Linking values to actions for wild pollinator conservation: perspectives in Europe
affiliations: French National Institute for Agriculture, Food and Environment (INRAE), University of Cambridge, Independent and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Linking values to actions for wild pollinator conservation: perspectives in Europe
detail.abstract: Pollinator declines challenge societal values and priorities in Europe. This study captures how such values intersect with policy preferences. We examine diverse perspectives of key stakeholder groups from business, policy, research and NGOs in Europe to investigate the underlying value systems and motivations that can drive pollinator conservation actions. The identified perspectives reveal variation in how individuals understand pollinators, their perception on pollinator values and how they conceptualise (ir)relevant pollinator conservation responses. This offers a more nuanced understanding of the sociocultural drivers of biodiversity management. While all perspectives acknowledged the importance of pollinator conservation to some extent, they diverge in the values they prioritize and the actions they support. Perspectives on actions differed in how they conceptualised the role of governance and authority — ranging from moral obligations to protect all species, to instrumental arguments for maintaining pollination functions. Correlations between different perspectives on values and actions show distinct patterns. Those with relationship-centred values (focused on balancing social needs) tended to prefer top-down regulations. Nature-centred intrinsic values (focused on ethical considerations) supported both alternative technical solutions and bottom-up awareness efforts. A perspective emphasizing all-species equality favoured top-down regulations and opposed horizontal coordination and collaboration. In contrast, those with human-centred values (highlighting the benefits of pollinators for food production and ecosystem services) preferred non-intervention and supported horizontal collaboration. Discussion highlights implications for the design, legitimacy, and transformative potential of conservation initiatives.

title: The Profile of Human Sporotrichosis: A Socioepidemiological and Spatial Approach Six Years After Mandatory Notification in Minas Gerais, Southeastern Brazil
affiliations: Federal University of Minas Gerais (UFMG), affiliation not provided to SSRN, Federal University of Minas Gerais (UFMG), affiliation not provided to SSRN, Federal University of Minas Gerais (UFMG), affiliation not provided to SSRN, Prefeitura de Belo Horizonte/PBH, Universidad de Guanajuato, Universidad de Guanajuato, Federal University of Minas Gerais (UFMG) and Federal University of Minas Gerais (UFMG)

detail.title: The Profile of Human Sporotrichosis: A Socioepidemiological and Spatial Approach Six Years After Mandatory Notification in Minas Gerais, Southeastern Brazil
detail.abstract: The sporotrichosis epidemic has significantly impacted public health across Brazil, including Minas Gerais. This study describes the epidemiological evolution of human sporotrichosis during the first six years of mandatory reporting (2018-2023) in the Minas Gerais state. A total of 2,351 confirmed cases were recorded, mostly diagnosed by clinical-epidemiological criteria (68.7%). Cases predominantly affected women (67.2%), individuals of brown ethnic group (47.7%), and those with a median age of 42.5 years. Spatial analysis revealed a consistent territorial expansion, with all mesoregions reporting cases, by 2023; central and southeastern regions were most affected. Incidence rates varied widely (0.46 to 165.51/100,000 people). Most affected municipalities had higher Municipal Human Development Index scores (62%) and were small-sized (44.56%). Our study highlights critical issues related to local social and spatial factors, underscoring the need to develop more effective surveillance and control strategies at both regional and municipal levels.

title: Monetary policy and supply-side turnover
affiliations: University of College London and Deutsche Bundesbank

detail.title: Monetary policy and supply-side turnover
detail.abstract: The introduction of a firm or product life cycle into New Keynesian frameworks fundamentally alters the design of optimal monetary policy. Economic welfare and the Phillips curve then depend on the gap between inflation and a time-varying inflation target that arises endogenously from turnover. The inflation target is positive on average and shifts in response to productivity disturbances. As a result, steady-state price stability is no longer desirable and the dynamics make it optimal for monetary policy to “look through” certain productivity disturbances. The latter requires keeping nominal rates unchanged even though both output and inflation move. This complicates the empirical distinction between supply, demand, and policy shocks. Our results highlight that accounting for supply side turnover delivers a rich set of policy-relevant results for inflation targeting and shock identification.

title: תקנת השוק במכר על ידי רשות שנפל בהליכיו פגם חוקי Market Overt in Judicial and Execution Sales: The Intersection of Property, Administrative and Execution Law

detail.title: תקנת השוק במכר על ידי רשות שנפל בהליכיו פגם חוקי Market Overt in Judicial and Execution Sales: The Intersection of Property, Administrative and Execution Law

detail.abstract:
תקציר בעברית: מאמר זה עוסק בתקנת השוק במכר על ידי רשות ודן בשאלה אם יש להחילה כאשר נפל פגם חוקי בהליכי המכר. לצד דיון מעמיק בדיני הקניין, שאלה משפטית זו מחייבת דיון נרחב בשתי דיסציפלינות משפטיות נוספות: המשפט המנהלי ודיני ההוצאה לפועל. ההכרעה בשאלה זו הינה בעלת השפעה רבה, עקב הכמות הרבה של מכירות שמבצעות רשויות המדינה, חשיבותן לאינטרס הציבורי והפגמים הרבים אשר, למרבה הצער, נוטים ליפול בהן. כמו כן, לניתוח המשפטי של הסוגיה ערך רב לאור עמימות הדין המצוי העולה מן הפסיקה, המתבטא בהימנעות בית המשפט העליון מהכרעה בנושא ובמגמות משתנות וסותרות בבתי המשפט המחוזיים.

במאמר אפרוס רקע על גלגולי תקנת השוק במכר על ידי רשות ואתאר באופן ביקורתי את הדין המצוי, ומתוך כך אדון בדין הרצוי במסגרות המשפטיות השונות. מבחינת דיני הקניין, ייטען כי כדי לשמור על תכלית תקנת השוק יש להחילה גם כאשר נפל פגם חוקי בהליכי המכר של הרשות. מסקנה זו תיתמך בהשוואה לתקנות שוק אחרות וכן בשיקולי יעילות. לצד זאת, יוצע מנגנון המעדן את הפגיעה בבעלים המקורי, המאפשר לו לפדות את נכסו האבוד למשך שנה מעת המכירה.

מבחינת המשפט המנהלי, אטען כי אף על פי שעקרון חוקיות המנהל עלול להביא לבטלות המכר, על תקנת השוק לחול כיוון שביכולתה להגן גם על זכות בטלה. כלומר, בהתנגשות החזיתית בין דיני הקניין למשפט המנהלי הנבחנת במאמר, גוברים דיני הקניין. לצד זאת, תוצג דרישה מחודשת מן הרשות עבור החלת תקנת השוק – דרישת תום הלב. כן תידון האפשרות לתבוע את הרשות המוכרת, גם כאשר מדובר ברשות שיפוטית.

מבחינת דיני ההוצאה לפועל, ייטען כי יש להפריד מבחינה מהותית וכרונולוגית בין תקנת השוק ובין סמכותו החריגה של רשם ההוצאה לפועל לבטל את המכר בשל הפגמים שנפלו בו. עקב כך, מרגע שתחול תקנת השוק, ברישום העסקה במרשם המקרקעין, אין בסמכות הרשם לבטל את המכר עקב הפגם החוקי שנפל בהליכיו.

Also, the general conditions of volatility and risk in the Italian equity market compared to US and Europe and the trends observed in government bond markets are examined. title: Multiple Equilibria? Don’t Panic! – A Hitchhiker’s Guide to Global Games

detail.title: Multiple Equilibria? Don’t Panic! – A Hitchhiker’s Guide to Global Games
detail.abstract: This article provides a practical overview for applying the global games approach to solve models with multiple equilibria that are often used in discussions on financial and macroprudential policies. Global games offer a tractable approach to resolve multiple equilibria by introducing incomplete information, thereby yielding unique equilibrium predictions. The article proceeds along the lines of a simple regime change game with strategic complementarities. Starting from the canonical regime change game with homogeneous players, it extends the discussion to include heterogeneous groups of players and interlinkages across different institutions with different sets of players. These extensions highlight not only how strategic complementarities can amplify fragility across players and institutions but also how heterogeneity and interlinkages affects the design of micro and macroprudential policy interventions. Finally, the article briefly discusses the application of global games to dynamic coordination games.

title: Development Index: A Quantitative Description of Civilisation

detail.title: Development Index: A Quantitative Description of Civilisation
detail.abstract: This report introduces the Development Index, a novel quantitative framework for assessing the level of societal development beyond traditional, often binary classifications. The Index measures a society's level of global connectivity by synthesising human infrastructure and organisational complexity. It models a society's journey through distinct civilisational stages, each defined by a specific, transformative process that enhances collective coordination and individual agency. Addressing the need for a continuous and reliable measure that transcends narrow economic metrics, this work formulates a holistic index composed of existing and novel indicators spanning economic prosperity, social inclusivity, environmental sustainability, and cultural openness. The resulting framework provides a mathematically rigorous, transparent methodology for understanding societal advancement as the progressive realisation of systemic integration and social synergy through increasing interconnectedness.

title: No Detectable Economic Effect of Extreme Heat After Correcting for Dependence
affiliations: Independent and University of Pennsylvania - Statistics Department

detail.title: No Detectable Economic Effect of Extreme Heat After Correcting for Dependence
detail.abstract: Callahan and Mankin (2022, 2025) argue that extreme heat, measured by the maximum 5-day average temperature (Tx5d), exerts a detectable and economically meaningful impact on subnational GDP per-capita growth. In doing so, they complete the causal chain at the heart of the increasingly important area of climate attribution science, which links producers of greenhouse gasses to economic damages. We show that Callahan and Menkin's result does not hold up when analyzed by methods that properly respect the data's pronounced spatial and temporal dependence. We report four main findings: first, we show that C&M's "placebo" (permutation) assessment of model is invalid since it breaks the scountry-year spatial/temporal correlation structure. When we implement country-preserving permutations that preserve this structure and a post-selection correction factor, statistical significance disappears. Second, we show that CM's results depend on few influential countries and years and removing them collapses the estimated Tx5d effect and even flips signs in some cases, reversing the direction of the economic effect. Third, we fit a novel hierarchical Bayesian model with region-within-country structure and AR(1) year effects, which show much larger uncertainty, shrinks the effect by 67-90%, and have credible intervals span zero. Finally, we implement rolling out-of-sample prediction tests with both i.i.d. and blocked cross-validation, which show that adding extreme climate variables does not improve predictive accuracy over models without them. We conclude that there is no measurable effect of extreme temperature events on GDP growth in the C&M data once the correlation structure, model selection, and outliers are handled correctly.

title: The Effect of Poverty on COVID-19 Infections in the United States

detail.title: The Effect of Poverty on COVID-19 Infections in the United States

detail.abstract: This paper examines whether poverty influences the spread of COVID-19 infections in the United States. Using state-level data from the U.S. Census Bureau and the New York Times, I estimate spatial lag and spatial error models to account for geographic spillovers in infection rates. The analysis focuses on two periods-January and April 2021-and employs four alternative model specifications. Across all models, poverty is not statistically associated with COVID-19 infection rates during the study period. In contrast, education is negatively related to infections, while income shows a positive association in cross-sectional specifications. Spatial dependence is strong and persistent, indicating that COVID-19 spread is highly correlated across neighboring states. When modeling changes in infection rates over time, only spatial dependence remains significant, suggesting that socioeconomic factors explain cross-sectional variation but not the evolution of infections. These findings highlight the importance of accounting for spatial dynamics when designing public health policies to address pandemic spread.

title: Afro-Atlantic Energy Corridors as Geo-Economic Development Architectures: A Phased Framework for Continental Interconnection, Industrial Anchoring, and Transatlantic Cooperation

detail.title: Afro-Atlantic Energy Corridors as Geo-Economic Development Architectures: A Phased Framework for Continental Interconnection, Industrial Anchoring, and Transatlantic Cooperation
detail.abstract: This paper proposes the Africo-Atlantic Project (PAA) as a geo-economic development architecture that reframes energy infrastructure from a transport asset into a platform for continental integration, industrial transformation, and transatlantic cooperation. The project is structured in phased form around two backbone gas corridors: (i) the Nigeria-Morocco corridor along Africa's Atlantic façade, designed to supply regional markets and connect to Europe via existing Mediterranean interconnectors; and (ii) an extension corridor linking Nigeria to Southern Africa, conceived as a novel mechanism for continent-wide energy interconnection and industrial scaling. Beyond energy security, the framework positions corridors as instruments of industrial anchoring-enabling processing industries, fertilizer and agro-industrial value chains, and integrated logistics/port development across participating states. The paper advances a governance-first perspective, arguing that large-scale corridors require a modular institutional architecture combining intergovernmental coordination, financing platforms, and a structured academic pillar (consortia, research chairs, and corridor living labs) to secure legitimacy and implementation capacity (World Bank, 2018; Asian Development Bank, 2021). The contribution is twofold: conceptually, it introduces the Afro-Atlantic basin as an under-theorized integration space for corridor-based development; operationally, it provides a phased roadmap, governance design, and partnership model to engage development banks and multilateral institutions. The analysis targets policy and investment audiences and offers a basis for future empirical evaluation of corridordriven industrial outcomes. The paper provides a programmatic development framework rather than engineering specifications or causal impact estimates.

title: Frictional Macroeconomics: A Unified Framework for Real-Time Policy and Measurement

detail.title: Frictional Macroeconomics: A Unified Framework for Real-Time Policy and Measurement
detail.abstract: This paper introduces a unified theoretical framework-Frictional Macroeconomics-that systematically incorporates four fundamental frictions shaping modern economies: (1) information frictions (rational inattention), (2) measurement frictions (lags and errors in official statistics), (3) financial frictions (balance sheet constraints), and (4) dynamic frictions (multi-scale economic cycles). The framework is microfounded from first principles and validated across 15 advanced economies (1960-2025) and U.S. Treasury auctions (2000-2025). A central contribution is the explicit distinction between ex-post explanatory power (what happened) and real-time forecasting ability (what can be predicted), together with quantitative bounds on each. The Generalized Phillips Curve with endogenous attention weights reduces ex-post measurement errors by 23.1% and ex-post GDP nowcasting errors by 27.9%; however, real-time forecasting improvements are more modest (10-15%) due to regime-identification lags. We provide: (1) a methodology for real-time regime classification using only lagged information, (2) explicit parameter-stability tests to guard against overfitting, and (3) bounds on expected performance degradation in genuine real-time applications. The framework delivers operational tools while transparently acknowledging implementation challenges.

detail.abstract: By deriving the Laplace transform of asset return covariance, we can convert asset return data into the spectral return resonance in the frequency domain. title: Should the Green End Justify All Means? A Critical Analysis of Recent Environmental Measures in EU VAT Law through the Lens of Equality

detail.title: Should the Green End Justify All Means? A Critical Analysis of Recent Environmental Measures in EU VAT Law through the Lens of Equality

publicationDetails.detailsText: European Law Review, Volume 50, Issue 3 (2025), pp. 259-273

detail.abstract: Current imperatives in the face of the climate crisis have led the European Union (EU) legislator to introduce environmental rate measures in value added tax (VAT) law. While the importance of addressing the challenges of climate change is undeniable, it should not be forgotten that related policies result in direct and/or indirect advantages for (certain) green business activities in the Member States. Such a reality is notoriously in some tension with the idea of an internal market characterised by a free play of market forces. Therefore, environmental measures in EU VAT law must be properly drafted, so that their legal design is consistent with the objective they seek to achieve and they can hence be considered as acceptable market interventions. Given that these environmental measures, by their very nature, distinguish between different groups of competing business operators, the EU principle of equal treatment emerges as a particularly relevant yardstick for such an assessment. By analysing recent measures under Directive 2022/542 in the light of art.20 of the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union (the Charter), this article sheds light on critical aspects of the legal design of environmentally inspired EU VAT legislation through the lens of equality.

detail.abstract: This study presents an end-to-end framework for automated factor discovery in cryptocurrency markets using GPT-5.2. Using USD-quoted perpetual contracts on BitMEX, we generate alpha factors via zero-shot generation and few-shot iterative enhancement. The top long-short factor delivers 658.01% annualized excess return with a Sharpe ratio of 4.13, and we find that leading signals remain robust in a strictly forward out-of-sample window defined by the model's training cutoff, even during a sharp downturn. Cross-model comparisons (GPT, Gemini, Grok) suggest that frontier LLMs can internalize and operationalize crypto-specific market microstructure logic-especially liquidity-leverage traps-rather than merely fit historical correlations. We also document important boundary conditions: few-shot refinement can increase complexity and overfitting, and distinct-looking factors may be logically redundant, motivating explicit redundancy control in generative factor mining.

title: The Fiduciary Duties of Network Participants of Blockchain Systems
affiliations: European University Institute - Robert Schuman Centre for Advanced Studies (RSCAS) and Université Paris II - Panthéon-Assas

detail.title: The Fiduciary Duties of Network Participants of Blockchain Systems

declarations.funderStatement: This research is funded by the European Research Council (ERC) under the European Union’s Horizon 2020 Research and Innovation Programme (Grant Agreements No. 865856).

publicationDetails.detailsText: Werbach, K. Micheler, E, Kremer, B. (eds.) Foundations of Decentralized Organisations, Oxford University Press

detail.abstract:
As blockchain technologies and cryptocurrencies transition from experimental niches to critical infrastructure, their social and economic impacts have sparked intense regulatory and judicial scrutiny. Central to this debate is the legal classification of network participants—including developers, founders, and governance token-holders—and the extent of their legal obligations to the public and one another.

This paper examines the burgeoning trend of courts and scholars to characterize these relationships as fiduciary in nature or to categorize Decentralized Autonomous Organizations (DAOs) as general partnerships. Analyzing key litigation such as Tulip Trading Ltd. in the UK and recent DAO-related rulings in the US, we explore the significant risks of joint and several liability and nationwide personal jurisdiction that now face industry participants.

We argue that the imposition of implicit fiduciary duties on blockchain participants is fundamentally improper. Such a move misapplies traditional corporate legal doctrines to decentralized architectures, risks stifling technological innovation, and may deter the broad-based participation essential to these systems. Drawing on our experience developing the COALA DAO Model Law (2022), we advocate for a shift away from status-based duties. Instead, we propose a co-regulatory approach grounded in the principle of regulatory equivalence. By prioritizing system-wide transparency, accountability, and novel governance frameworks, regulators can protect public interests without compromising the core principles of decentralization and autonomy.

detail.title: Gold Standards for Price Discovery
detail.abstract: This paper analyzes price discovery in the gold markets, an ideal empirical benchmark for such analysis: spot, futures and ETF markets interact strongly and continuously. We use a structural framework, allowing for a clear identification of permanent and transitory components. Such perspective solves the apparent contradictions sometimes observed between price discovery measures in the empirical literature. Using one-minute midquotes from 2021-2024, we show and explain how measures evolve over time. Analyzing daily estimates without smoothing reveals insight into stable and volatile periods, as well as a structural break in late 2022 also seen in structural parameters. Bootstrap inference further confirms or invalidates the statistical significance of measures, differences and structural parameters. Finally, we make the R code available 1 to facilitate replication and further research.

title: The Hidden Cost of Pay Transparency
affiliations: University of Macau and Peking University HSBC Business School

detail.title: The Hidden Cost of Pay Transparency
detail.abstract: This paper studies how U.S. pay transparency laws affect firms' employment policies and longterm growth. Exploiting the staggered adoption of state laws requiring salary disclosure in job postings, which reduce workers' search costs and strengthen their outside options, we provide causal evidence on firms' responses to heightened retention pressure. We show that greater pay transparency lowers employee satisfaction through intensified cross-firm comparisons, particularly regarding career opportunities and workplace attributes. Firms respond by increasing labor retention through higher wages and enhanced non-wage benefits, including longer tenure and greater use of remote work. These effects are stronger among financially flexible and employment-friendly firms, as well as firms located in states with weak non-compete enforceability and more generous unemployment insurance benefits. We find no evidence that these retention efforts operate through changes in hiring, worker productivity, or within-firm wage dispersion. Instead, higher labor retention costs crowd out investment, leading to weaker innovation, slower long-term growth, and lower firm value. Our findings reveal an unintended consequence of pay transparency laws: gains in labor market transparency come at the cost of reduced firm efficiency due to distorted internal resource allocation.

title: Supply Constraints and Negative Selection: Evidence from Mental Healthcare Markets

detail.title: Supply Constraints and Negative Selection: Evidence from Mental Healthcare Markets
detail.abstract: Despite universal healthcare coverage and clinical guidelines recommending psychotherapy after psychiatric hospitalization, only 26% of German patients receive it, and paradoxically, the sickest patients are least likely to get treatment. Using administrative claims data, we investigate whether increasing psychotherapy supply addresses this misallocation. For identification, we exploit quasi-random variation from Germany's therapist license allocation system. A one standard deviation higher supply raises therapy uptake by 10%, modestly reduces waiting times, and lowers patient search frictions, but does not alter the composition of therapy recipients. These findings challenge the assumption that healthcare capacity constraints affect all patients equally.

title: The Evaluator Age: Generative AI and the Future of Knowledge Work
affiliations: University of Connecticut, University of Connecticut - Department of Operations & Information Management and University of California, Davis

detail.title: The Evaluator Age: Generative AI and the Future of Knowledge Work

keywords: Enterprise AI governance and analytics models

detail.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence is dramatically reordering knowledge work, propelling organizations from the Producer Age into what we term the Evaluator Age. In this emerging phase, human value lies not in generating content but in critically assessing, refining, and ethically stewarding machine outputs. We trace the progression from the Preserver Age-when humans safeguarded scarce knowledge-through the Producer Age of mass creation, to today's evaluator imperative. Generative models now excel at first-draft production, shifting the strategic bottleneck to quality control, bias detection, and contextual fit-tasks uniquely served by professionals who blend deep domain expertise, AI literacy, and moral judgment. We argue that universities must redesign curricula accordingly, foregrounding evaluative competencies alongside technical fluency. By positioning graduates as skilled custodians of AI-generated insight, higher education can secure its relevance and ensure that organizations harness AI responsibly and effectively.

title: Unemployment Insurance, Wage Pass-Through, and Endogenous Take-Up
affiliations: University of Georgia,  and U.S. Census Bureau

detail.title: Unemployment Insurance, Wage Pass-Through, and Endogenous Take-Up
detail.abstract: This paper studies how unemployment insurance (UI) generosity affects reservation wages, re-employment wages, and benefit take-up. Using Benefit Accuracy Measurement (BAM) data, we estimate a cross-sectional elasticity of reservation wages with respect to weekly UI benefits of 0.014. Exploiting state variation in Pandemic Unemployment Assistance (PUA) intensity and the timing of federal supplements, we find that expanded benefits during Covid-19 increased reservation wages by 8-12 percent. Using CPS rotation data, we also document a 9 percent rise in re-employment wages for UI-eligible workers relative to ineligible workers. Over the same period, the UI take-up rate rose from roughly 30 to 40 percent; Probit estimates indicate that higher benefit levels, rather than changes in observables, account for this increase. To interpret these findings, we develop a directed search model with an endogenous filing decision. The model shows that large benefit expansions primarily operate through the extensive margin of take-up, expanding the pool of claimants in ways that dampen the observed pass-through from benefits to wages.

title: Enterprise-Scale Data Quality Improvement Using Machine Learning: Frameworks, Validation Strategies, and Operational Insights

detail.title: Enterprise-Scale Data Quality Improvement Using Machine Learning: Frameworks, Validation Strategies, and Operational Insights
detail.abstract: Enterprises operating at scale increasingly depend on accurate, consistent, and trustworthy data to support analytics, regulatory reporting, operational execution, and strategic decision making, yet traditional rule-based data quality programs have struggled to keep pace with rising data volumes, heterogeneous data sources, and rapidly changing business conditions. This study addresses the persistent gap between static data validation techniques and the dynamic error patterns that emerge within modern enterprise platforms by developing and evaluating machine learning driven frameworks designed to identify, classify, and prioritize data quality issues with higher precision and adaptability. Using a mixed methodological approach that integrates architectural analysis, quantitative experimentation, and scenario-oriented evaluation, the research examines how supervised learning models, probabilistic classifiers, and feature engineered validation pipelines can outperform conventional rule sets in detecting anomalies, missing values, inconsistent records, and entity level conflicts across complex datasets. Findings demonstrate that machine learning models achieve substantial gains in accuracy, recall, and operational robustness, while also improving the interpretability of validation decisions when embedded within structured enterprise workflows. The study presents innovative validation strategies that combine predictive modeling with governance-oriented feedback loops, enabling organizations to respond to evolving data behaviors and reduce downstream operational risks. By contributing reference architecture, empirical benchmarks, and applied insights, the research advances both academic understanding and industry practice in enterprise data quality management. The results indicate that machine learning enabled validation provides a scalable and future ready foundation for enterprises seeking to strengthen trust in data assets and enhance the resilience of data dependent operations.

title: AI Marketing Agents for Multi-Location Restaurants: Operational Design, Performance Metrics, and Strategic Implications

detail.title: AI Marketing Agents for Multi-Location Restaurants: Operational Design, Performance Metrics, and Strategic Implications
detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence is increasingly embedded in marketing technology, yet most applications remain focused on task automation or channel-level optimization. This paper argues that the primary impact of AI in marketing lies instead in its capacity to function as a governed decision system that coordinates marketing actions at scale. Focusing on multi-location restaurant organizations, the paper develops a conceptual framework that positions AI marketing agents as decision actors embedded within marketing technology systems. Building on post-2018 research in organizational AI, marketing analytics, and platform theory, the paper articulates an operational design based on bounded autonomy, separation of decision intelligence from execution, continuous learning, and human oversight. It further proposes a performance measurement framework that evaluates AI marketing agents in terms of decision quality, coordination effectiveness, governance compliance, and organizational impact rather than channel-specific outcomes alone. The paper concludes by discussing strategic implications for marketing technology platforms, multi-location marketing strategy, and the evolving role of marketing management.

detail.abstract: This article defends a structurally counterintuitive thesis: revolutions function historically as adaptive mechanisms for systemic survival rather than emancipatory ruptures. Instead of destroying systems of power, they facilitate the substitution of defunct elites, rationalized institutional reconfigurations, and technological upgrades to social control—preserving the underlying logic of domination. Through materialist, realist, and elitist analysis of comparative history, I argue that revolutions operate as symbolic resets restoring system legitimacy at the cost of violence, transitional instability, and emancipatory illusion. Mass mobilization supplies the raw force; circulating elites determine institutional outcomes. The belief in revolution as rupture may itself be a mechanism of systemic stability.

title: Constitutional AI Ethics: Education for Democratic Deliberation in the Age of AGI

detail.title: Constitutional AI Ethics: Education for Democratic Deliberation in the Age of AGI

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author of this publication declares there are no competing interests.
declarations.funderStatement: This research was supported by the Strategic Research Council (No. 358250).

detail.abstract: As artificial intelligence capabilities approach generality (AGI), the possibility space of achievable futures expands. Societies face irreducibly normative questions: which futures should we pursue? Legitimate resolution in democratic societies requires collective deliberation by those who must live with consequences. Yet the capabilities such deliberation demands remain unspecified. This paper conceptualizes four capabilities that such deliberation requires: constitutional reasoning, trade-off reasoning, impartial reasoning, and internal governance efficacy, derived from the structural requirements of democratic legitimacy. I introduce constitutional AI ethics education as the approach for cultivating them, enabling citizens to participate meaningfully in determining which AGI-enabled futures to pursue, what lives are worth living, and what it means to exist well together. This is human subjectivity under AGI conditions: not outperforming artificial intelligence at cognitive tasks but existing as beings capable of determination itself. Constitutional AI ethics education represents what socialization to democratic order means under AGI conditions: the institutional preparation that makes democratic self-governance possible when the futures to be governed remain genuinely undetermined. Without this expansion of education, directional questions will be answered by those with the power to decide rather than those who must live with the consequences. This paper establishes the conceptual foundation for education that cultivates citizens who can deliberate about AGI-enabled futures, rather than merely inhabiting arrangements given.

detail.abstract: AI systems are increasingly trained to optimise performance without explicit visibility into how decision authority and responsibility are structured.
